confidence.rationale: Major contemporary motivation frameworks define these constructs separately and assign them different theoretical roles.

limitations: The distinctions do not establish one complete taxonomy or one universal causal sequence.

scope.population: Humans choosing or pursuing goals in declared contexts.
scope.temporal_scope: Before, during, and after a bounded action opportunity.

claims.statement: Motivation must distinguish expected success, subjective value, intrinsic and autonomous reasons, controlled pressure, effort cost, actual opportunity, observable persistence, and performance rather than treating them as one quantity.

confidence.rationale: The large meta-analysis covered school, work, and physical domains, but most relations are predictive rather than randomized causal contrasts and constructs and outcomes were heterogeneous.

claims.confounding_note: Ability, prior achievement, opportunity, task selection, common-method measurement, incentives, role demands, and domain can contribute to observed prediction.

estimate.notes: Intrinsic motivation predicted performance at approximately rho = .21 to .45 across analyses; incentive and outcome moderators changed the pattern.

limitations: The result does not show that rewards always help, always undermine intrinsic motivation, or cause durable engagement.

boundary_conditions: Performance quality, performance quantity, and direct versus indirect incentive salience are distinguished.
scope.population: 212,468 participants represented in 183 school, work, and physical-domain studies.
scope.temporal_scope: Source-specific motivation assessment, incentive condition, and performance period.

claims.statement: Across 183 studies, intrinsic motivation and extrinsic incentives both predicted performance, with intrinsic motivation more predictive of performance quality and incentives more predictive of quantity.

causal_assumptions.consistency: SDT interventions contained heterogeneous component combinations and are not one uniform treatment.
causal_assumptions.exchangeability: Randomization supports baseline exchangeability within trials; attrition and selective reporting can compromise it.
causal_assumptions.interference: Generally assumed; group and social-support components may create interaction.
causal_assumptions.positivity: Included trials contained intervention and control conditions.

claims.causal_estimand: Average difference in prespecified health behavior between assignment to an SDT-informed intervention and its declared control condition.

confidence.rationale: Randomized comparisons support an average effect, but the pooled interventions and behaviors were heterogeneous and publication and small-sample bias reduced the corrected estimate.

estimate.notes: Bias-corrected effects remained positive but smaller, at least d = .15 in reported corrections.

limitations: The average effect does not establish effectiveness for every behavior, component, person, or context.

boundary_conditions: Health behavior, intervention components, comparator, delivery, population, and follow-up must match a represented or sufficiently similar context.
scope.population: Participants in randomized health-behavior intervention trials represented in 56 articles and 65 independent tests.
scope.temporal_scope: Postintervention health behavior and source-specific follow-up.

claims.statement: Across 65 independent randomized tests, Self-Determination-Theory-informed interventions produced a small average improvement in health behavior relative to control conditions.
claims.temporal_ordering: Intervention assignment preceded motivational assessments and later behavior.

confidence.rationale: The source tested theory-specified mediation across randomized interventions, but aggregate mediation and heterogeneous measurement do not identify a within-person causal pathway.

indirect_effect.notes: Autonomous motivation and perceived competence statistically mediated intervention effects in the reported MASEM.

limitations: Statistical mediation does not prove that changing autonomous motivation caused behavior change in a particular person.

scope.population: Participants represented in randomized SDT health-behavior intervention trials.
scope.temporal_scope: Intervention assignment, motivational assessment, and later health behavior as represented in the synthesis.

claims.statement: Meta-analytic structural equation modeling linked SDT interventions to health behavior partly through measured autonomous motivation and perceived competence.
claims.temporal_ordering: Randomization preceded outcomes, but mediator timing and mediator-outcome confounding were not uniformly established across trials.

confidence.rationale: Most included studies were randomized or cluster randomized and effects were positive, while intervention bundles, populations, risk of bias, and meta-regression uncertainty limit component-level claims.

claims.confounding_note: The pooled set mixed randomized, cluster-randomized, and nonrandomized controlled designs, and intervention bundles and implementation quality differed.

estimate.notes: Reported pooled effects included autonomy support g = .84, autonomy g = .81, competence g = .63, relatedness g = .28, and motivation g = .41.

limitations: The synthesis did not show that one isolated technique reliably produces all changes or that self-report change guarantees sustained behavior.

scope.population: Children and adults represented in 74 controlled health-intervention studies.
scope.temporal_scope: Pre-post motivational assessment during health interventions.

claims.statement: Across 74 controlled health interventions, need-supportive programs improved perceived autonomy support, autonomy, competence, relatedness, and motivation measures on average, with heterogeneous effects and limited evidence for any single technique.

confidence.rationale: Expectancy-value theories organize substantial observational and intervention evidence, but the complete within-person integration and computation are not directly identified as one universal mechanism.

claims.falsifiable_boundary: The account is weakened when independently changing expectancy, value, or cost fails to alter subsequent choices as predicted and when competing process models better predict held-out within-person behavior.
limitations: The hypothesis must not be used to explain any action after the fact without prospective measurements and competing models.

boundary_conditions: Expectancy, value, cost, opportunity, skill, action, and outcome are measured separately.
scope.population: Humans choosing or pursuing goals with measurable alternatives, expectancies, values, costs, actions, and outcomes.
scope.temporal_scope: Appraisal before choice, followed by effort, outcome, and possible updating.

claims.statement: Goal selection and persistence may arise from a situated integration of expected success, subjective value, effort and opportunity costs, alternatives, social context, and prior experience.
claims.temporal_ordering: Candidate expectancy, value, and cost appraisals precede the measured choice or persistence period.

evidence.design: Random-effects meta-analysis of intrinsic motivation, extrinsic incentives, and performance across school, work, and physical domains.

effect.notes: Intrinsic motivation predicted performance at rho = .21 to .45; unique prediction differed for quality versus quantity and incentive salience.

evidence.extraction_locator: PubMed abstract reporting k = 183, N = 212,468, corrected correlations, performance-quality and quantity moderators, and incentive salience.
limitations: Prediction across heterogeneous studies does not establish a universal causal effect of changing motivation or incentives.
evidence.summary: Intrinsic motivation and incentives jointly predicted performance, with different relevance for quality and quantity.

evidence.design: Random-effects meta-analysis of randomized SDT-informed health-behavior intervention trials.

effect.notes: Small average behavior effect; bias-corrected effects remained positive but smaller.

evidence.extraction_locator: PubMed abstract reporting 56 articles, 65 independent randomized tests, d+ = .23, behavior-specific effects, bias analyses, and corrected effects.
limitations: Publication bias, small-study bias, intervention heterogeneity, and behavior-specific effects limit generalization.
evidence.population: Participants represented across 65 independent randomized tests.
evidence.summary: SDT-informed interventions produced a small average improvement in health behavior across randomized tests.

evidence.design: Meta-analytic structural equation modeling nested within a synthesis of randomized SDT health-behavior interventions.

effect.notes: Autonomous motivation and perceived competence were reported as mediators.

evidence.extraction_locator: PubMed abstract description of meta-analytic structural equation modeling of autonomous motivation and perceived competence as mediators.
limitations: Aggregate path models do not establish within-person causal mediation or eliminate mediator-outcome confounding.
evidence.population: Participants represented in eligible randomized intervention trials with mediation variables.
evidence.summary: Autonomous motivation and perceived competence statistically accounted for part of the intervention-behavior relation.

evidence.design: Systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis of controlled SDT-informed health interventions reporting pre-post psychosocial mediators.

effect.metric: Hedges g for need-support and motivation outcomes
effect.notes: Positive pooled changes in autonomy support, autonomy, competence, relatedness, and motivation.

evidence.extraction_locator: PubMed abstract reporting 74 controlled studies, 80 percent randomized or cluster randomized, outcome-specific Hedges g estimates, and meta-regression of techniques.
limitations: Mixed controlled designs and co-occurring techniques prevent strong causal attribution to a single strategy.
evidence.population: Children and adults represented in 74 health-intervention studies.
evidence.summary: Need-supportive intervention bundles improved several motivation-related self-report measures on average.

evidence.design: Integrative theoretical review of situated expectancy-value research across developmental, social-cognitive, and sociocultural levels.
evidence.extraction_locator: Review sections defining expectancies, task-value components and cost, contextual influences, choices, persistence, and the warning that the model is not static or monolithic.
limitations: A theoretical synthesis organizes evidence but does not identify the full mechanism in one person.
evidence.population: Primarily children, adolescents, and adults represented in achievement-motivation research.
evidence.summary: Expectancies, values, costs, choices, and context form a useful process framework, but not one directly observed universal computation.

metadata.description: Separates motivation, expectancy, value, effort cost, intrinsic and autonomous motivation, controlled motivation, persistence, performance, interventions, and proposed integration mechanisms.
metadata.title: Evidence pack for motivation beyond reinforcement

boundary_notes: Motivation is not one amount, a stable moral quality, observed performance, pleasure, reward, intention, or willpower.
Similar behavior can arise from different values, pressures, habits, needs, expectancies, opportunities, or constraints.
objects.definition: Processes that energize, select, direct, and sustain action toward or away from anticipated outcomes in a particular person and context.
objects.label: Goal-directed motivation

boundary_notes: Expected success is not objective ability, actual opportunity, certainty, or guaranteed control over the outcome.
objects.definition: A person's context-specific expectation that a contemplated action can be performed and can contribute to the intended outcome.
objects.label: Expected success or efficacy

boundary_notes: Value is person-, goal-, time-, and context-specific and is not equivalent to external reward magnitude.
objects.definition: Context-sensitive importance, usefulness, interest, identity relevance, or anticipated benefit assigned to an activity or outcome, considered alongside its costs.
objects.label: Subjective task value

boundary_notes: Intrinsic motivation is narrower than autonomous motivation and does not make an activity beneficial, feasible, or morally preferable.
objects.definition: Motivation to perform an activity for its inherent interest or enjoyment rather than solely for a separable consequence.
objects.label: Intrinsic motivation

boundary_notes: Autonomous motivation does not mean independence from other people, unlimited choice, or absence of structure.
objects.definition: Motivation experienced with a sense of volition and ownership, including intrinsic motivation and well-internalized extrinsic reasons.
objects.label: Autonomous motivation

boundary_notes: Controlled motivation can produce behavior and is not identical to no motivation; its effects depend on task, contingency, duration, and outcome.
objects.definition: Motivation organized primarily around external demands, rewards, punishments, approval, shame, or internal pressure.
objects.label: Controlled motivation

objects.definition: A declared setting in which a person can choose, initiate, persist in, modify, or stop an action in relation to a specified goal and available alternatives.

dimensions.consequences: expected and experienced benefits, costs, and social responses
dimensions.opportunity: actual time, resources, skills, and access

objects.label: Bounded goal-pursuit context
objects.scope: Educational, work, laboratory, and health-behavior contexts represented in the included reviews.

boundary_notes: Perceived cost is not laziness and may reflect real fatigue, risk, pain, competing obligations, inaccessible design, or forgone alternatives.
objects.definition: Time-varying anticipated or experienced burden of allocating physical, cognitive, emotional, social, or temporal resources to an action rather than alternatives.
objects.label: Perceived effort and opportunity cost

objects.definition: Observable allocation of action, time, repetitions, or task engagement toward a declared goal across one or more opportunities.
objects.function_note: Low persistence can reflect low value or expectancy, high cost, competing goals, insufficient skill, environmental barriers, fatigue, or adaptive disengagement.
objects.label: Goal-directed effort and persistence
objects.response_topography: Source-specific task choice, initiation, time on task, repetition, persistence, or disengagement.

boundary_notes: A self-report score is not direct observation of effort, value integration, need satisfaction, or a unique causal mechanism.
objects.definition: A declared scale or item set estimating intrinsic, autonomous, controlled, amotivated, expectancy, value, competence, or need-support constructs.
objects.label: Motivation and regulation self-report
objects.method: Report construct, instrument, items, timeframe, language, scoring, reliability, respondent, and context.

boundary_notes: Performance combines motivation with ability, knowledge, strategy, health, opportunity, and measurement conditions.
objects.definition: Protocol-defined record of task choice, initiation, time, repetitions, disengagement, quality, quantity, or goal attainment.
objects.label: Effort, persistence, and performance measurement
objects.method: Declare task, opportunities, alternatives, time window, quality and quantity criteria, incentives, barriers, and missingness.

objects.definition: A structured intervention intended to support volition, competence, or relatedness through combinations of meaningful rationale, noncontrolling language, choice within boundaries, skill support, feedback, and social connection.
objects.delivery: Source-specific health behavior intervention informed by Self-Determination Theory and compared with a declared control condition.
objects.label: Need-supportive motivation intervention

boundary_notes: More behavior is not automatically better; the goal, consent, safety, quality, sustainability, and competing outcomes must be declared.
objects.definition: Prespecified behavioral or performance result occurring after the motivational assessment or intervention.
objects.label: Goal-relevant behavior or performance

boundary_notes: A multiplication metaphor or path diagram is not direct evidence that one universal computation caused a person's action.
objects.definition: Proposed process in which expected success, subjective value, effort and opportunity costs, alternatives, social context, and prior experience jointly influence action selection and persistence.
objects.label: Situated expectancy-value-cost integration
realization_conditions: Expectancy, value, cost, alternatives, opportunity, action, and result are measured separately in the same context.
Candidate inputs precede the relevant choice or persistence period.
Competing habit, affective, social, reinforcement-learning, skill, and barrier explanations remain testable.

sources.authority_note: Contemporary theory review used to separate expectancy, value, cost, context, choice, and persistence without treating the diagram as a proven static mechanism.
sources.title: From expectancy-value theory to situated expectancy-value theory — a developmental, social cognitive, and sociocultural perspective on motivation

sources.authority_note: Contemporary SDT review used for construct definitions and theory boundaries, not as causal evidence for every proposed need pathway.
sources.title: Intrinsic and extrinsic motivation from a self-determination theory perspective — definitions, theory, practices, and future directions

sources.authority_note: Large cross-domain meta-analysis used for bounded predictive relations among intrinsic motivation, incentives, and performance.
sources.title: Intrinsic motivation and extrinsic incentives jointly predict performance — a 40-year meta-analysis

sources.authority_note: Randomized-trial meta-analysis used to distinguish intervention effects from statistical mediation and complete mechanism identification.
sources.title: Self-determination theory interventions for health behavior change — meta-analysis and meta-analytic structural equation modeling of randomized controlled trials

sources.authority_note: Controlled-intervention meta-analysis used for motivation and need-support outcomes while preserving bundle and component uncertainty.
sources.title: A meta-analysis of techniques to promote motivation for health behaviour change from a self-determination theory perspective
